title: Officer takes the stand
article: The Winnipeg police officer who fatally shot 18-year-old Matthew Dumas says, he had no other choice but to pull the trigger.
Friday, Constable Dennis Gburek took the stand at the inquest into Dumas' death. It was the first time the Dumas family heard from the officer who killed Matthew.
Gburek told the inquiry he feared getting stabbed in the neck when he first saw robbery suspect, Matthew Dumas, on Dufferin Avenue. Dumas was carrying a screwdriver when police cornered him.
Gburek said he thought it was a knife at first, but realized it was a screw driver as he approached.
He says he yelled at Dumas to drop the screwdriver. As Dumas got closer, he yelled, "stop, I'm going to shoot."
He describes how Dumas had an angry look in his eyes, and how he saw the teen getting pepper-sprayed by another officer.
Lawyers also questioned Gburek about his firearms training, and whether he has regrets about his actions, to which he replied no.
Five more police officers involved in the shooting are expected to take the stand next week. T he inquest continues M onday.
